mātūrē

adverb · Wiktionary

early, in good time

Earlier than usual is the comparative mātūrius. Early in the morning is bene māne (see very early); in good time, temperī (see in good time). Gellius records that mātūrē properly meant “at the right moment, neither too soon nor too late” (Gell. 10.11.2).

Other words

  • mātūrius — earlier (than usual)

    adverb (comparative of mātūrē) · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.19.2: parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius; Caes. BG 4.6: mātūrius … proficīscitur (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

  • praemātūrē — too early, too soon

    also used · classical · Traupman 308 · Wiktionary

Examples

  • invītat Canius postrīdiē familiārēs suōs, venit ipse mātūrē

    the next day Canius invites his friends, and comes early himselfCic. Off. 3.59

  • Aesōpus dominō sōlus cum esset familia, parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius

    Aesop, being his master’s only servant, was told to get dinner ready earlier than usualPhaedr. 3.19.1–2

See also early, very early, it’s too early, in good time, late.
